title: Biaxial nematics and nematic-nematic demixing in polydisperse mixtures of hard board-like particle fluids
authors: Yuri Martinez-Raton, Daniel de las Heras, Enrique Velasco
abstract: We study the bulk phase behavior of a polydisperse liquid crystal fluid made of biaxial boards with restricted orientations using both fundamental measure theory and Monte Carlo computer simulations. The continuous polydispersity is included in the intermediate particle length of the boards via a truncated Schulz distribution. By calculating several phase diagrams across a range of polydispersity coefficients, we find that polydispersity (i) enhances demixing between two uniaxial nematic phases and (ii) expands the stability region of the biaxial phase. Although metastable with respect to non-uniform phases, we identify certain mixtures exhibiting two-phase coexistence paths involving uniaxial-uniaxial and uniaxial-biaxial phase separations. Whether these paths can be completed depends on the precise shape of the parent distribution function. Monte Carlo simulations performed for a representative case exhibit the same phase diagram topology predicted by theory, thereby validating the theoretical approach. The main difference between both approaches lies in quantitative agreement, with simulated phase transitions systematically occurring at higher packing fractions than those predicted theoretically. Our combined theoretical and simulation results may prove relevant to the design and interpretation of sedimentation experiments on colloidal suspensions of polydisperse anisotropic particles.
summary: This work theoretically and computationally examines how polydispersity affects the phase transitions, particularly nematic-nematic demixing, in fluids of hard, biaxial board-like particles. Using Fundamental Measure Theory and Monte Carlo simulations, the authors show that size variation stabilizes the biaxial phase and enhances demixing regions. The results provide a detailed understanding of phase coexistence paths relevant to colloidal science.
main_problem: The study investigates the bulk phase behavior, specifically nematic-nematic demixing, in polydisperse mixtures of hard board-like particle fluids.
main_result: Polydispersity enhances demixing between uniaxial nematic phases and expands the stability region of the biaxial phase. The theoretical predictions are validated by Monte Carlo simulations, though quantitative differences exist.
method: The authors employ Fundamental Measure Theory (FMT) density functional theory alongside Monte Carlo (MC) computer simulations to model the system's phase behavior.
model_or_system: The system is a polydisperse liquid crystal fluid composed of hard biaxial boards with restricted orientations. Polydispersity is modeled using a truncated Schulz distribution for the intermediate particle length.
key_observables: Phase diagrams, weighted densities, chemical potential, and the degree of size fractionation.
important_parameters: Polydispersity coefficient, particle dimensions ($\sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3$), and packing fractions ($\eta_0$).
main_assumptions: The theoretical approach is compared against MC simulations, and the completion of two-phase coexistence paths depends on the precise shape of the parent size distribution function.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing $	ext{B-Np}$ and $	ext{B-Nr}$ coexistence paths as a function of parameters like $\eta_0$ and $\sigma_0$, demonstrating first-order transitions.
paper_structure: The paper develops the FMT framework for polydisperse systems, calculates equilibrium moments for single and two-phase coexistence, and validates the resulting phase diagram topology using MC simulations, focusing on the impact of polydispersity.
why_interesting: While focused on classical colloidal systems, the rigorous application of density functional theory and phase diagram construction techniques for complex, anisotropic, and polydisperse matter is highly relevant to understanding phase transitions in many-body quantum systems.
